# fixed field　`def.fixed-field`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.fixed-field)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.fixed-field.md)

In the Galois correspondence for a finite Galois extension, $H \mapsto L^{H}$ and the intermediate field $M \mapsto \operatorname{Gal}(L/M)$ are mutually inverse (see `thm.galois-correspondence`).

## Notes · **draft**
⭐ Reverse inclusion: $H_1 \subseteq H_2 \implies L^{H_2} \subseteq L^{H_1}$ — the larger the group, the fewer objects it fixes.

⭐ Examples: the conjugation automorphism of $\mathbb{C}/\mathbb{R}$ generates a group of order $2$, whose fixed field is $\mathbb{R}$; for the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}/\mathbb{F}_p$, the fixed field of the group generated by Frobenius is $\mathbb{F}_p$.
